transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um... well, I'm here because things are just... slipping, I guess. At work. I'm a software developer, but I also handle some patent stuff, workshop prep, team decisions... and lately, I just can't seem to organize all the moving parts anymore. I end up just doing whatever is loudest or most urgent instead of what actually matters. It's... getting to be a problem.
Have you struggled with this kind of disorganization and difficulty focusing your entire life, or is this a relatively new development for you?

Um... I guess it's not exactly new. Looking back... it was there in grade school, too. My teachers used to write that I was bright, but... that I daydreamed a lot. I'd actually finish my assignments and then just... forget to turn them in. Or I'd lose my homework folders entirely. That was all long before I was even a teenager. So... yeah. It's been a while, I suppose.
Beyond the difficulty with organization and focus, do you feel like you are constantly 'on the go' or find it difficult to sit still for long periods, like in meetings or while watching a movie?

Um... I wouldn't really say I'm always on the go. But... sitting still can be tough sometimes. 

Like on long design calls... I start getting this... pressure building up in my body to just get up. I usually end up pacing around my office, or... shifting from chair to chair. Even when I'm just trying to look focused on the screen. So... yeah. I guess I do that.
When you are in those meetings where you feel the urge to pace, do you find that you also frequently interrupt others or blurt out answers before they have finished speaking?
Um... no, not really. I don't think I do that. I mostly just... keep to myself on those calls. I don't really talk over people or... blurt things out. I just wait until they're done, I guess.
In your daily life, how often do you find yourself losing things that are necessary for your work or daily tasks, such as keys, glasses, phones, or important documents?

Um... yeah. Quite a bit, actually. 

I guess I'm... constantly hunting for things I need for work. Like my USB-C adapters, or... my stylus. My sketchbook. Sometimes even my work badge. It... well, it can derail a whole morning, honestly. I just... I have no memory of where I set them down. So... yeah. That happens.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting with your hands or feet, or squirming in your seat when you are expected to stay seated for long periods?

Um... no. Not really. 

I don't... I don't think I do that. Like I mentioned, I usually just get up and pace if I need to. But... as far as just sitting there and squirming or fidgeting with my hands... I haven't really noticed doing that. So... no.
When you are working on tasks that you find boring or repetitive, do you often find your mind wandering or that you struggle to keep your attention on the work?
Um... I don't know. Maybe? I guess my mind wanders sometimes, but... I haven't really thought about it. I just try to get the work done.
When you are in situations where you are expected to remain seated, do you often find that you feel internally restless or unable to relax, even if you aren't physically squirming or fidgeting?

Um... I guess so. Like... on long design calls. 

I just get this... pressure building up in my body to get up. So I usually end up pacing around my office. Or... I'll just shift from chair to chair. Even when I'm, you know, trying to look focused on the camera. So... yeah. I suppose I do feel that.
